title: Lesson 2: BLESS Rhythms - Living on Mission Every Day
description: Five practical rhythms for living on mission where you live, work, and play: Begin with Prayer, Listen, Eat, Serve, Story. Not a program - a way of life.

blocks.text: In Lesson 1 you drew your Personal Ministry Map and wrote down the people God has placed around you. You are sent. The next four lessons give you a simple way to live that out on an ordinary Tuesday: the BLESS rhythms. Begin with Prayer, Listen, Eat, Serve, and Story. They are habits, not a program, and they turn the places where you already live, work, and play into places of mission. This lesson starts where every rhythm starts, with prayer. Lesson 3 covers Listen and Eat, Lesson 4 covers Serve, and Lesson 5 covers Story.

blocks.alt: BLESS - Begin with Prayer, Listen, Eat, Serve, Story

blocks.title: A Prayer Before the Answer
blocks.text:
Nehemiah had a good job in a palace a long way from home. He was cupbearer to Artaxerxes, king of Persia, which meant he stood near the most powerful man in the world every day. Then his brother arrived with news from Jerusalem. The walls were broken down, the gates were burned, and the people there were in great trouble and shame.

Nehemiah did not rush in to fix it. He wept, and then he prayed. "As soon as I heard these words I sat down and wept and mourned for days, and I continued fasting and praying before the God of heaven" (Nehemiah 1:4). Day after day he carried those people to God, and he asked for one thing for himself: success, and "mercy in the sight of this man" when the moment came (Nehemiah 1:11).

The moment came about four months later. Nehemiah was serving the king, and the king noticed his face. "Why is your face sad, seeing you are not sick?" (Nehemiah 2:2). Nehemiah was afraid. Then the king asked, "What are you requesting?" Before he answered, Nehemiah did one more thing: "So I prayed to the God of heaven" (Nehemiah 2:4). Then he spoke, and the king said yes. Nehemiah knew exactly why: "the good hand of my God was upon me" (Nehemiah 2:8).

Notice the order. Nehemiah talked to God about his people for months before he talked to the king about them. All that praying made him ready for a conversation he could never have planned, and when it came, a quick, silent prayer carried him through it. That is the first BLESS rhythm. Talk to God about people before you talk to people about God.
2.1 - Nehemiah carried his people to God long before he ever spoke up for them. Who is someone you care about but rarely pray for?
Why Prayer Comes First

Mission is God's work before it is yours. Jesus said, "My Father is working until now, and I am working" (John 5:17). Long before you notice your neighbor, God already knows their name, their story, and what keeps them up at night. Prayer is how you find out where He is working and join Him there. It is also how He changes your eyes, so the people you have been walking past start to look like people He loves.

First of all, then, I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all people... This is good, and it is pleasing in the sight of God our Savior, who desires all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.

Praying for the people around you has two motions, like breathing. You breathe in by listening to the Father. Jesus did this often: "he would withdraw to desolate places and pray" (Luke 5:16). Ask Him two simple questions: God, where are You already working in the places I live, work, and play? How can I join You? Then you breathe out by praying for people and places by name, asking God to bless them and draw them to Himself.

2.2 - Write the names of three to five people from your Personal Ministry Map who do not yet follow Jesus. These are your people to pray for daily. What do you know about each of them that you can bring to God this week?
Your Prayer Card

A simple tool helps you pray for each name with more than a quick "bless them." Write your names on a card, in a note on your phone, or on the back of your Ministry Map. Then pray three things for each person.

blocks.title: Their Life, Their Heart, My Part
content: Their life. Pray for what they are carrying right now: health, family, work, money, a hard decision. Pray the way you would want a friend to pray for you.
Their heart. Pray that God would draw them to Himself and open their eyes to Jesus. Only He can do that (John 6:44), so ask Him boldly.
My part. Pray that God would open a door, give you eyes to notice it, and give you the courage and kindness to walk through it.

blocks.text: Carry it in one phrase: their life, their heart, my part. It is simple enough to sketch on a napkin, and it keeps your prayers personal, centered on the gospel, and honest about your part.
Making Prayer a Rhythm

Prayer for neighbors grows best when it is tied to something you already do. Pray your names while the coffee brews, on your commute, or when you pull into the driveway. Set a daily reminder on your phone. Some people take a prayer walk, quietly praying for each home they pass or each desk at work. You do not need a quiet hour. You need a few honest minutes, most days.

Prayer also happens in the middle of life. Like Nehemiah in front of the king, you can pray a short, silent prayer in the middle of a conversation: Lord, help me listen. Give me the right words. Sometimes the simplest open door is a question: "How can I pray for you?" Many people, even those far from faith, welcome a sincere offer like that. If it feels natural, pray with them right then in a sentence or two. Then write it down and ask them about it next week. Few things say "I care" like remembering.
Continue steadfastly in prayer, being watchful in it with thanksgiving. At the same time, pray also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, to declare the mystery of Christ.
2.3 - When and where in your normal day will you pray for your names? Be specific: the time, the place, and what will remind you.
Prayer Is Not a Performance

You might read this and remember every time you said "I'll pray for you" and then forgot. Take heart. Prayer is not a test you pass to stay in God's good graces. You come to the Father because Jesus has already made the way, and Jesus Himself is praying for His people right now: "he always lives to make intercession for them" (Hebrews 7:25). You pray for your neighbors as someone who has been prayed for. When you miss a day, do not quit. Just begin again.
Over time, prayer leads into the rest of BLESS. The people you pray for become the people you listen to, eat with, serve, and in time share your story with.
2.4 - Look back at your names from question 2.2. For each person, which next step feels most natural: listening more, sharing a meal, serving them, or sharing your story?
Lesson 2 Review

Every BLESS rhythm begins with prayer, because mission is God's work before it is yours. Like Nehemiah, you talk to God about people before you talk to people about God. Pray most days for three to five names, using a simple pattern: their life, their heart, my part. Ask God where He is already working and how you can join Him, then watch for the doors only He can open.
In the next lesson, you will learn the next two rhythms, Listen and Eat, and how an open table can turn a name on your prayer card into a friend.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
The BLESS rhythms are adapted from BLESS: 5 Everyday Ways to Love Your Neighbor and Change the World by Dave Ferguson and Jon Ferguson.
